item: A launcher row that cannot get the lock in time is written by a detached child under that lock, never without it (R174)
summary: Under CPU load (4 CPUs, 8 busy loops) the 30 ms wait of R173 timed out on 168 of 240 contended calls and the row, appended without the lock, was lost to a holder's trim in 15 of 240 (measured). Now a launcher that cannot get the lock inside its wait (bash 100 ms, PowerShell 520 ms: the longest append-plus-trim holds measured under that load, 92.4 ms and 515.0 ms, pinned by a test naming the load) hands the row to a detached child and carries on at once; the child waits for the same lock with no time bound, then does the locked append and the trim if due, writes nothing before it holds the lock, leaves no file behind and never has the row in a command line (the PowerShell child is started with ONE fixed script and gets the path, the limits and the row on its standard input; the bash child keeps the row in its memory) and ends when the holder does (flock released by the kernel, the mkdir lock by dead-pid takeover, the Mutex by abandonment). The ONE way a row can still be late is a holder that is alive and stuck for ever; a machine that goes down before the child writes loses the row. Deferred rows can land after later rows, so launcher_stderr now orders its lines by the rows own time, not their place in the file. Same 8-way run under load: bash helper 240 rows 0 lost with 113 deferred, launchers bash exits 40 and stops 40 and PowerShell exits 32 rows 0 lost. Deterministic red-without: a holder that trims slowly while a second launcher times out loses the row on the R173 build and not now (flock and mkdir lock), plus the PowerShell mutex twin. Two launchers ending together with a trim due, 200 rounds, bash: the build before R173 lost 20 of 400 rows, this build 0 of 400 (below about 0.75 % at 95 % confidence, not proved zero; PowerShell not run at 200 rounds). Rows byte-identical, no new bytes. Also folds two ruff items of this stack (UP037 in vllm_lifecycle, I001 in test_session_forensics_budget). On a bash without BASHPID (3.2) the mkdir lock records the launcher pid and not the child pid; never run on macOS.
